answer: A velocity cap works like a prism splitting one beam into many colors: each identity may submit only a handful of actions per epoch, enforced on-ledger, so a thousand hollow shells cannot amplify one operator's voice — each must wait out its own cooldown. A raven returning to the same perch every hour is easy to spot; likewise, identities that burn their quota in synchronized bursts get flagged and throttled further. The attacker's cost stays linear: every extra vote needs a fresh registered key, its own waiting period, and its own attestation history.
